label: cor:finite-dicritical-plane
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:finite-dicritical-plane}
Let $\mathcal F$ be a codimension-one holomorphic foliation on $\mathbb P^2$, and
let
\(
M\subset\mathbb P^2
\)
be an irreducible real-analytic variety of pure real codimension one  invariant by $\mathcal F$. Assume
that
\(
\operatorname{Sing}(M)\subset\operatorname{Sing}(\mathcal F).
\)
Let $p_1,\ldots,p_r\in M\cap\operatorname{Sing}(\mathcal F)$ be all the dicritical singularities
and, for each $j$, let
\[
H_j:(U_j,p_j)\dashrightarrow\mathbb P^1
\]
be a local meromorphic first integral of the germ
$(\mathcal F,p_j)$. Assume that every Levi leaf $L\subset M_{\mathrm{reg}}$
accumulates at least one of the points $p_j$.

Assume that, for every $j$ and every generic global Levi leaf $L$
approaching $p_j$, the restriction $H_j|_{L\cap U_j}$ is constant;
denote its value by
\[
\lambda_j(L)\in\mathbb P^1.
\]
Assume moreover that there exist transformations
\[
A_{ji}\in\operatorname{PGL}(2,\mathbb C)
\]
depending only on the pair $(i,j)$, and not on the Levi leaf, such that
whenever a generic global Levi leaf $L$ accumulates at both $p_i$
and $p_j$ one has
\[
\lambda_j(L)=A_{ji}\bigl(\lambda_i(L)\bigr),
\]
and that the transformations satisfy
\[
A_{ii}=\operatorname{id},
\qquad
A_{kj}\circ A_{ji}=A_{ki}
\]
whenever all terms are defined.

Then $\mathcal F$ admits a nonconstant rational first integral on $\mathbb P^2$.
head: environment
name: Finite dicritical set in $\PP^2$

title: Proof
body_md:
By hypothesis every Levi leaf accumulates at least one of the
dicritical points $p_1,\ldots,p_r$. Starting from a local first
integral $H_j$ at any such point reached by a given leaf, the
constancy condition makes the holonomy continuation single-valued
near that leaf. The projective compatibility maps $A_{ji}$ and their
cocycle relations identify these local continuations whenever their
domains overlap. They therefore glue to a meromorphic first integral
on a neighborhood of $M_{\mathrm{reg}}$.

At each $p_j$ the corresponding normalized local first integral
extends the glued function meromorphically through $p_j$. Any
remaining singular point of $\mathcal F$ on $M$ is non-dicritical and is
treated by Lemma~\ref{lem:nondicritical}. Thus the first integral is
meromorphic on a neighborhood of all of $M$.

The local pseudoconvexity argument of Section~\ref{sec:pseudoconvexity} and the meromorphic
extension argument on the complementary Stein domains globalize this
function to $\mathbb P^2$. The resulting global meromorphic function is
rational.

body_md:
This is the special case of Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-dicritical-plane} with $r=1$.
Equivalently, Proposition~\ref{prop:nearMreg} gives the first integral
near $M_{\mathrm{reg}}$, the local first integral at $p$ supplies the
extension at the only dicritical singularity, and
Lemma~\ref{lem:nondicritical} treats the remaining singular points.
The projective extension argument then gives a rational first

title: Example
body_md:
The elementary rational pencil
\(
R=\frac{z_0}{z_1}
\)
on $\mathbb P^2$ preserves
\(
M=\overline{R^{-1}(\mathbb RP^1)}.
\)
The unique dicritical point is
\(
p=[0:0:1],
\)
and the Levi leaves are
\[
z_0-\lambda z_1=0,\qquad \lambda\in\mathbb RP^1.
\]
Thus Corollary~\ref{cor:single-dicritical-plane} applies.

title: Proof
body_md:
Assume first that $\mathcal F$ admits a primitive rational first integral
\(
R:\mathbb P^2\dashrightarrow\mathbb P^1.
\)
Choose a smooth real-analytic Jordan curve
\(
\gamma\subset\mathbb P^1
\)
of regular values of the resolved rational map and set
\(
M=\overline{R^{-1}(\gamma)}.
\)
The generic fiber is connected and, over regular values of the resolved
map, smooth; hence the corresponding Levi leaves are the connected
fibers over $\gamma$. The hypersurface $M$ is invariant by $\mathcal F$ and is
smooth away from the base locus of the pencil. Let
$p_1,\ldots,p_r$ be all dicritical base points of $R$ belonging to $M$.
For each $j$, take
\(
H_j=R|_{U_j}:(U_j,p_j)\dashrightarrow\mathbb P^1.
\)
These local meromorphic first integrals need not be minimal; this is why
minimality is not imposed in condition \textup{(ii)}. On every generic
global Levi leaf $L$, each $H_j$ is constant wherever $L$ approaches
$p_j$, with value equal to the global value $R(L)$. Thus we may take
\(
A_{ji}=\operatorname{id}
\)
(after using the same global coordinate on the target $\mathbb P^1$ for all
$j$), and all compatibility conditions in \textup{(ii)} follow.

Conversely, assume \textup{(ii)}. The local constancy and projective
compatibility hypotheses are precisely the hypotheses required by
Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-dicritical-plane}; its proof uses only the
chosen local meromorphic first integrals and does not require their
minimality. Hence $\mathcal F$ admits a nonconstant rational first integral
on $\mathbb P^2$. Replacing it by the primitive generator furnished by the
Stein factorization of the associated rational map gives a primitive
rational first integral.
